title: Strain- and potential-controlled tunneling in monolayer MoS$_2$
authors: Hasna Chnafa, Rachid El Aitouni, Clarence Cortes, David Laroze, Ahmed Jellal
abstract: We present a theoretical study of spin- and valley-resolved quantum transport in monolayer MoS$_2$ under the combined influence of mechanical strain and an external scalar potential, a combination whose simultaneous unexplored. Within an effective massive Dirac Hamiltonian that incorporates intrinsic spin--orbit coupling, strain induces valley-dependent momentum shifts that lift the degeneracy between the $K$ and $K'$ valleys and strongly modify the transport characteristics. The scalar potential modifies the tunneling spectrum, leading to pronounced changes in resonant transmission, Fabry--Pérot interference, and conductance. We show that the interplay between strain and electrostatic potential enables efficient control of both valley and spin polarization of the transmitted current. In particular, we identify a dual-knob control scheme in which the barrier width governs the frequency of conductance oscillations while strain independently controls their phase and amplitude. Furthermore, we predict electrostatic spin inversion -- a sign reversal of spin polarization achievable purely by gate tuning at finite strain, requiring no geometric reconfiguration. Depending on the strain orientation, the transmission probability and conductance can be selectively suppressed or enhanced, resulting in highly tunable valley- and spin-polarized transport. These findings demonstrate that strain and potential engineering provide orthogonal and independently operable mechanisms for controlling conductance as well as spin and valley degrees of freedom in monolayer MoS$_2$, offering promising prospects for spintronic and valleytronic device applications.
summary: The paper theoretically explores how combining mechanical strain and electrostatic potentials can precisely control spin and valley polarization in monolayer MoS2. By analyzing quantum transport through engineered potential barriers, the authors predict a dual-knob control scheme that allows for independent tuning of conductance oscillations using these two external fields. This offers a powerful platform for realizing advanced spintronic devices.
main_problem: The study investigates spin- and valley-resolved quantum transport in monolayer MoS2 when subjected to the simultaneous influence of mechanical strain and an external scalar potential, a combination previously unexplored.
main_result: The interplay between strain and electrostatic potential allows for orthogonal control over both valley and spin polarization, enabling phenomena like 'electrostatic spin inversion' purely via gate tuning.
method: Theoretical analysis using an effective massive Dirac Hamiltonian incorporating intrinsic spin-orbit coupling to model electron transmission through a barrier region.
model_or_system: The system is monolayer MoS2 modeled by an effective Hamiltonian that includes terms for Fermi velocity, band gap, spin-orbit coupling, and strain. The transport calculation involves solving coupled differential equations across regions defined by the potential barrier and strain field.
key_observables: Spin polarization ($P_s$), valley polarization ($P_v$), resonant transmission probability ($T_{	au s_z}$), and total conductance ($G$).
important_parameters: Mechanical strain ($\epsilon$), electrostatic potential barrier height ($V_0$), barrier width ($L$), and incident energy ($E$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a continuum effective Dirac Hamiltonian, neglects higher-band corrections or intervalley scattering, and ignores disorder effects.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the MoS2 sheet under uniaxial strain and an external scalar electrostatic potential. Figure 11 shows spin polarization vs. strain for various barrier widths and energies.
paper_structure: The paper develops the Hamiltonian incorporating strain and potential, derives transmission coefficients using boundary matching conditions across three distinct regions (outside/inside/outside the barrier), and analyzes how varying parameters controls spin/valley polarization via quantum interference effects.
why_interesting: This work demonstrates highly tunable control over fundamental quantum degrees of freedom (spin and valley) in a 2D material using external fields, which is central to developing next-generation spintronic and valleytronic devices.
